# 600 second per-test deadline: a job ki: A configured deadline, not a reading. 600 seconds is the per-test timeout pyproject.toml SETS, and it means the same 600 seconds on every machine, so there is no measurement here for a machine to be named against. The sentence is about why this job's own cap has to be larger than it.
# anything under 5ms, so without it a fi: A threshold in pytest's own `--durations` reporting, not a reading. It is the number below which pytest declines to print, and it is the same on every machine.
# assumed 300 seconds a call and conclud: A figure the PLAN assumed and this tool refutes, and the sentence says so. It is also an Anthropic API round trip rather than local work, so the machine is not what decides it (the network and the model are).
# for at all, and to staying well under: A configured cap, not a reading. `timeout-minutes: 45` is a number this file SETS, and it means the same 45 minutes on every machine, so there is no measurement here for a machine to have produced.
# on, which is a different design from t: A timestamp INSIDE a video, not a duration of work: 0.6s is where in the reel the reference frame is taken from. It is the same instant of the same clip whatever machine renders it.
#: The tail of a pytest summary line: `i: Two examples of the TEXT this regular expression parses, quoted so the shape can be read. They are illustrations of a format, not measurements of anything.
#: largest shard against the 1,800 secon: A configured deadline, not a reading. 1,800 seconds is the value check_guards.py is GIVEN by the workflow, and it means the same 1,800 seconds on every machine, so there is no measurement here for a machine to be named against.
